claims.text: Both the dashi oden and the signature white-miso (Fuchu miso) oden are built on traditional Japanese seasonings; miso and oden broths conventionally contain wheat (miso koji and wheat-based soy sauce), so the food should be treated as containing gluten.
Oden simmers all ingredients together in shared fish dashi alongside oysters, anago, beef and chicken items, so vegetable items are not free of animal products.
Anagomeshi and oyster dishes at this kind of eatery are conventionally prepared with Japanese soy sauce / tare, which contains wheat; no gluten-free preparation is documented.

name: 花山椒 八丁堀店 (Hanasansho Hatchobori-ten)

claims.text: The shop specializes in wheat-noodle brothless dan dan noodles dressed in sesame or seafood-based sauces; such Japanese sauces conventionally contain wheat-based soy sauce, though no allergen statement is published.
Okonomiyaki is cooked on a single shared iron griddle alongside wheat noodles, wheat-flour batter, and wheat-based okonomi sauce, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent to the cooking method.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki is finished with a wheat-based okonomi/soy sauce; no gluten-free or wheat-free sauce is documented.
The griddle is continuously used for pork, beef, egg, and seafood including oysters, so any item would share surface with animal products.
As a small single-counter wok kitchen serving noodles, dumplings and fried rice, shared woks, soy-based seasonings and wheat ingredients make cross-contact with gluten effectively unavoidable.
Standard Japanese/Chinese soy sauce (which normally contains wheat) is used throughout the cooking.
Vegetable dishes are prepared in the same wok and seasonings as meat, egg and seafood dishes, so cross-contact with animal products is likely.
The kitchen centers on wheat noodles for both tsukemen and ramen, so flour and wheat-based broth are present throughout; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The dipping sauce and seasonings use standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
Broth is made with bonito (fish) dashi and dishes include chashu pork and egg, so animal products are integral to the kitchen.

name: 広島赤焼 えん 駅西本店 (Hiroshima Akayaki En Ekinishi Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki and teppan izakaya dishes here are finished with standard wheat-based okonomiyaki/soy sauces; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
